core_summary: Animals carry out vital life processes including nutrition (ingestion, mechanical and chemical digestion, absorption, assimilation, egestion) and respiration (breathing and cellular oxidation of glucose). In humans, food travels through the alimentary canal (mouth, esophagus, stomach, small intestine, large intestine, rectum, anus). Small intestine villi absorb broken-down nutrients into blood. Respiration breaks down glucose with oxygen yielding CO2, water, and ATP energy. Specialized adaptations exist in other animals (rumination in cattle, gill respiration in fish). Historical Ayurvedic text Charaka Samhita emphasized digestive health.
key_concepts: To measure and compare human breathing rates during rest versus after intense physical exercise.

key_terms.definition: Glucose + Oxygen -> Carbon Dioxide + Water + Energy (ATP).

key_takeaways: Breathing is a physical mechanical process of gas exchange (O2 in, CO2 out). Respiration is a biochemical cellular process releasing ATP energy from glucose oxidation.
